record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: In cases where the nonlinear evolution ∂_t f(z,t) = z f′(z,t) ∫_T ((z+ζ)/(z-ζ)) |dζ| / |f′(ζ,t)|^α is well posed, what geometric information can be proved about the resulting hulls K(t)? In particular, do their boundaries have any regularity, and is the evolution stable under perturbations of the initial conformal map φ?

evidence.quote: In instances where we do have existence and uniqueness, can the geometric features of the hulls K(t) be described and analyzed? Do the boundaries have any degree of smoothness? Do we have stability in the initial condition, in the sense that if the initial map φ is perturbed, then the resulting evolution is close to the unperturbed one, in some suitable sense?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk and $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$ the unit circle. Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, and let $\varphi:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a univalent (conformal) map with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $\varphi'(0)>0$. Consider the family of univalent maps $f(\cdot,t):\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}\setminus K(t)$ (with $f(\cdot,0)=\varphi$) governed by the nonlinear Loewner-type evolution
$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(z,t)\;=\;z\,f'(z,t)\int_{\mathbb{T}}\frac{z+\zeta}{z-\zeta}\,\frac{|d\zeta|}{|f'(\zeta,t)|^{\alpha}},\qquad z\in\mathbb{D},$$
where $f'$ denotes the derivative in $z$ and the boundary values $f'(\zeta,t)$ are understood in a suitable (e.g., nontangential) sense. The increasing family of compact "hulls" is $K(t)=\mathbb{C}\setminus f(\mathbb{D},t)$.

In any regime in which this evolution is well posed (existence and uniqueness of $f(\cdot,t)$ on some time interval $[0,T)$), establish geometric properties of the hulls $K(t)$. Specifically:

(a) Prove or disprove that for $t\in(0,T)$ the boundary $\partial K(t)$ enjoys some degree of regularity (for example, that it is a Jordan curve, locally connected, Hölder, or smoother), and identify the optimal regularity as a function of $\alpha$ and of the regularity of $\varphi$.

(b) Prove or disprove stability of the evolution with respect to the initial datum: if $\varphi_n\to\varphi$ in a suitable topology of conformal maps on $\mathbb{D}$, do the corresponding solutions $f_n(\cdot,t)$ converge to $f(\cdot,t)$ (equivalently, do the hulls $K_n(t)$ converge to $K(t)$, e.g., in the Carathéodory or Hausdorff sense) on the common interval of existence?
artifact.status_search_result: The specific nonlinear Loewner-type evolution with the $|f'(\zeta,t)|^{-\alpha}$ weight (a continuum analogue of Hastings–Levitov HL($\alpha$)) is studied actively, and partial results exist on related regularized models (scaling limits to Loewner–Kufarev equations, Hölder regularity of hull complements, stability in subcritical regimes). However, regularity and stability for this exact unregularized continuum equation, in the generality posed, do not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Regularized Hastings–Levitov Aggregation in the Subcritical Regime
status_evidence.snippet: Scaling limits and stability proven for a two-parameter class of regularized Hastings–Levitov models in the subcritical regime, with limit dynamics solving a Loewner–Kufarev equation.
status_evidence.claim: Stability/regularity results exist for regularized versions of HL(α), but not for the unregularized continuum evolution posed here.

status_evidence.title: Loewner traces driven by Lévy processes
status_evidence.snippet: Loewner hulls driven by Lévy processes are almost surely locally connected; complements are Hölder domains.
status_evidence.claim: Regularity results for related Loewner hulls are known, leaving the deterministic nonlinear case open.
